blocks.prompt: 11 (a) A person standing 20 meters away from the base of a tree measures the angle of elevation to the top of the tree as \(30^\circ\). Find the height of the tree.
blocks.explanation:
A right-triangle height problem: the tree, the ground and the line of sight form a right triangle.
Given the distance 20 m and the angle of elevation \(30^\circ\); find the height \(h\).
Plan: \(\tan 30^\circ = \frac{h}{20}\), then solve for \(h\).
steps:
Given: distance from the tree 20 m, angle of elevation \(30^\circ\).
To find: the height \(h\) of the tree.
Method: In the right triangle, the height is opposite the angle and the distance is adjacent, so use \(\tan\).

Solve for \(h\)
\[h = 20\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{20}{\sqrt{3}}\]
\[h = \dfrac{20\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 11.55 \text{ m}\]
Why: \(\tan 30^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\); rationalise and use \(\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732\).

Check
\[\tan^{-1}\tfrac{11.547}{20} = \tan^{-1}0.577 = 30^\circ\]
Why: The height gives back the measured angle.

blocks.prompt: 11 (b) A person standing 20 meters away from the base of a tree measures the angle of elevation to the top of the tree as \(30^\circ\). If the person walks 10 meters closer to the tree, what will be the new angle of elevation to the top of the tree?
blocks.explanation:
The tree's height stays the same; only the distance changes to \(20 - 10 = 10\) m.
Find the new angle of elevation \(\alpha\).
Plan: \(\tan\alpha = \frac{h}{10}\), then \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}\).
steps:
Given: \(h = \frac{20}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 11.55\) m (part (a)); new distance \(20 - 10 = 10\) m.
To find: the new angle of elevation \(\alpha\).
Method: Same right triangle idea, now with adjacent side 10 m.

Set up the equation
\[\tan\alpha = \dfrac{h}{10} = \dfrac{20/\sqrt{3}}{10}\]
\[\tan\alpha = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.1547\]
Why: Opposite \(= h\), adjacent \(= 10\) m.

Find the angle
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}(1.1547)\]
\[\alpha \approx 49.11^\circ \approx 49.1^\circ\]
Why: An angle of elevation is acute, so \(\tan^{-1}\) gives it directly (degree mode).

Check
\[10\tan 49.11^\circ = 10(1.1547) = 11.55\]
Why: This is the height of the tree. Walking closer makes the angle larger (\(30^\circ \to 49.1^\circ\)), as expected.
